Title: Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Says Wall Street Is 'Penalizing Hyperscalers' For Build-Out Costs, Ignoring Growth Potential
Author: Shivani Kumaresan   Tue, November 3, 2026 at 6:41 AM GMT+1 4 min read
Published: 2026-11-03T05:41:46+00:00
=== BODY ===
AI chip and hardware companies have led the market rally, with semiconductor stocks rising 44% and technology hardware stocks gaining 36%.
Meanwhile, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and Alphabet shares rose just 8% on average despite 27% earnings growth.
Pershing Square thinks investors and analysts are overlooking the potential for higher revenue and profits from hyperscalers.
Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Inc. (PS) believes Wall Street is underestimating the long-term potential of major technology companies investing heavily in artificial intelligence (AI), focusing too much on rising infrastructure costs while overlooking future revenue growth, stronger cash flows and returns. The investment firm also sees attractive opportunities across the broader stock market.
Pershing Square stock traded over 2% higher overnight, heading into Tuesday.
See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox
In its third-quarter letter to shareholders, Pershing Square noted that the S&P 500 advanced slightly more than 2% in Q3, but the typical company in the index fell 4%. More than 60% of its constituents ended the period lower. Through Sept. 30, the benchmark had climbed 13% for the year, while the average constituent gained just 1%.
Meanwhile, estimates for the median S&P 500 company's earnings per share rose 4% during the quarter and nearly 10% over the first nine months. Pershing Square said this disconnect has created opportunities to buy businesses whose underlying performance has improved despite weaker share prices.
According to Pershing, companies supplying semiconductors and technology hardware have benefited significantly from AI-related spending. The S&P 500 Semiconductor Index has advanced 44% this year, while the technology hardware index has gained 36%.
"The buildout of AI infrastructure has been one of the principal drivers of stock market performance this year, with the 'picks and shovels' companies having been the largest beneficiaries."
However, major cloud and technology companies, including Microsoft (MSFT), Meta Platforms (META), Amazon (AMZN) and Alphabet (GOOGL), have delivered an average share price increase of just 8%, despite reporting approximately 27% earnings growth.
"The decline in the hyperscalers' P/E multiples has largely been driven by investor concerns regarding the potential returns they will earn on their elevated capex spending."
The investment firm believes investors are overlooking the long-term benefits of heavy AI infrastructure spending. The four major tech companies could spend a combined $740 billion in 2026, up from $140 billion in 2023. Analysts expect that figure to exceed $1 trillion in 2027.
"We believe that the hyperscalers' capital spending is offensive rather than defensive. Rather than merely protecting existing franchises, we believe the hyperscalers are investing to accelerate growth and are deploying capital behind a transformative technology that plays directly to their competitive advantages."
"These include unmatched distribution, long-standing customer relationships, proprietary data and context, security and reliability at global scale, and the balance sheet strength to invest at a level few competitors can match."
The firm said Amazon's AI investment is boosting AWS growth, with revenue rising 39% in Q3. It is improving ad targeting and helping Meta grow revenue faster. Meta's Muse assistant crossed 10 million downloads within weeks, creating new opportunities to earn money through shopping, services, and business tools. AI is also creating growth opportunities through Azure, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and GitHub.
Analysts expect major technology companies to keep spending heavily on AI infrastructure for several years but do not expect their revenue growth to speed up much after this year and next. Pershing Square believes analysts are treating this spending as an ongoing cost rather than recognizing its potential to drive much higher future revenue and profits.
"In our view, analyst estimates penalize the hyperscalers for the cost of the buildout today while ascribing limited potential to the significant future growth in revenue and earnings that are likely to result from these investments."
The firm said much of the 2026 revenue growth comes from AI investments made in 2024 and 2025. So it expects current higher spending to drive even stronger growth in the coming years, potentially beating analysts' forecasts.
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained 'neutral'.

Title: Ben Cowen Says “Everyone Expects It” Was a Bad Reason to Bet Against the Q4 Market Selloff
Author: Darryn Pollock   Tue, November 3, 2026 at 6:12 AM GMT+1 2 min read
Published: 2026-11-03T05:12:00+00:00
=== BODY ===
Market analyst Benjamin Cowen says the Q4 market selloff in US stocks arrived on schedule, despite arguments that a widely expected correction would never happen.
The call rests on three midterm cycles, and Cowen says it is not an exact science. He says the Nasdaq has dropped over 10%, mirroring 2018. Bitcoin (BTC) holders face the same argument, since he says it also tends to bottom in Q4.
Cowen said in a video that he flagged the Q4 risk all year, while stressing it was never guaranteed.
He points to 2018, when he says stocks fell 23% late in the year. In 2022, he says, another drop of about 23% began in the third quarter.
According to Cowen, the Russell index has fallen 11% to 12% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average about 7%. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 has slipped about 4%.
Skeptics argued weeks ago that broad expectations would prevent the move. However, Cowen says the same objection preceded Bitcoin's lows in February and the summer.
He also points to Google's post-earnings slide as evidence the correction is real. Parent Alphabet closed 12.6% lower on Oct. 29, according to Trefis.
Cowen expects a low within the next couple of months, followed by a bounce. He sees the OpenAI IPO, which he guesses could come in early 2027, as the next major narrative.
Morgan Stanley strategist Mike Wilson, however, sees any dip as a buying opportunity. He says a drop toward 7,100 on the S&P 500 could precede a rally to 8,000.
The slide follows a 2.86% Nasdaq drop on Friday, and analysts have flagged midterm and AI risks this week.
Cowen says the Iran war and today's midterm elections add volatility. He expects the S&P 500 to be among the last to fall before a policy response from the administration.
The split tests whether broad expectations shield markets from seasonal drawdowns. For Bitcoin, the same test applies, as Cowen's earlier price warnings show.

Title: Stocks Rose a Year After Every Midterm Since 1982. Will 2026 Keep the Streak?
Author: Kamina Bashir   Tue, November 3, 2026 at 7:00 AM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-11-03T06:00:00+00:00
=== BODY ===
The S&P 500 has posted gains in the year after every US midterm since 1982. With Americans voting today, history favors stocks, but several macro risks could test that record.
Bitcoin (BTC) has also finished higher a year after recent midterms. However, its path through the following months has been far rougher than that of stocks.
According to CNBC, the S&P 500 averaged a 13.7% gain one year after the 11 midterm elections since 1982. The index ended higher in every case.
CFRA senior investment strategist Arun Sundaram points to an even longer record. He says markets have never fallen in the 12 months from October of a midterm year since World War II. Those periods averaged gains of about 16%.
"I think that the midterms are a bit of a clearing event. US markets tend to do better once we get past the midterms," Sundaram told CNBC.
Returns have also been larger when voters split control of Washington. Elections that left divided government saw an average 15% one-year gain, versus 11.5% under single-party control.
CFRA expects Democrats to take the House and likely the Senate. CNBC found a precedent for a Democratic Congress under a Republican president. After the 1986, 1990 and 2006 midterms, the S&P 500 averaged a 10.9% one-year gain.
Sundaram, however, says markets have historically done better under a Republican president and Congress than a Democratic one. He calls a Democratic sweep of Congress the worst case. Still, he says markets tend to be up 12 months later.
The calendar also favors stocks in the near term. Data shared by The Kobeissi Letter shows November has averaged a 2.1% gain since 1980, rising 74% of the time.
In midterm years since 1950, November has averaged 2.7%, with a 78.9% win rate.
Sundaram still calls geopolitics the big wild card this year, especially the war with Iran. CFRA raised its oil forecast and now expects prices to average about $85 a barrel next year, up from $70.
The 10-year Treasury yield slipped below 4.9% on Monday, down from a 5.3% high about a month earlier. Meanwhile, CNBC names artificial intelligence (AI) as the big swing factor now, and whether declines in tech will continue.
The midterm pattern has also appeared in crypto, though with far larger swings. Data from DWF Labs shows BTC rose 25%, 45%, and 92% a year after the 2014, 2018, and 2022 midterms.
However, BTC took a much rougher path than the S&P 500. It traded 31% below its election-day close three months after the 2014 vote and 46% below after 2018.
Whether either streak extends may depend on oil, yields, and AI as much as on the vote.

Title: Ford Just Gained 2% in a Month. Is It Time to Sell, or Load Up?
Author: Nikko Henson   Tue, November 3, 2026 at 8:25 AM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-11-03T07:25:57+00:00
=== BODY ===
Ford Motor (F) stock gained 2% in the month through October 30, with most of the increase following its third-quarter earnings report.
General Motors (GM) climbed 14% over the same period, supported by stronger profit growth.
Ford generated $4.7 billion in adjusted free cash flow during Q3 and raised its 2026 adjusted EBIT guidance floor to $10.5 billion.
At about 7x forward earnings with a 4.9% dividend yield, Ford looks undervalued despite expectations for a flat 2027.
Ford stock gained 2% in the month through October 30, with nearly all of the advance coming after its October 28 third-quarter earnings report.
GM performed considerably better, rising 14% over the same period. Ford nevertheless outperformed the broader market, as the S&P 500 declined 1% and the Nasdaq 100 fell 7%.
Ford reported adjusted EPS of $0.49, beating the $0.40 consensus estimate. Adjusted EBIT increased 3% year over year to $2.7 billion, supported by a smaller Ford Model e loss and a 27% increase in Ford Credit earnings, offsetting weaker results at Ford Blue and Ford Pro.
Cash generation was particularly encouraging. After producing just $220 million in adjusted free cash flow during the first half of 2026, Ford delivered $4.7 billion in Q3 and maintained its full-year guidance of $6 billion to $7 billion.
Ford expects 2027 profitability to remain roughly in line with 2026. Goldman Sachs lowered its price target from $14 to $12, Morgan Stanley reduced its target from $14 to $13, and RBC cut its target from $15 to $14.
CFO Sherry House said Ford expects "the next step function change in profitability" during the first half of 2028 as its electric vehicle platform and energy business ramp up.
TIKR consensus estimates as of October 20 projected normalized EPS of $1.84 in 2026 and $1.92 in 2027, representing approximately 4% growth.
These estimates predate Ford's latest results, but they suggest analysts were already expecting limited earnings growth in 2027.
GM's third-quarter EBIT-adjusted increased 22% year over year to $4.1 billion, compared with Ford's 3% growth.
GM also narrowed its 2026 EBIT-adjusted guidance to $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion, raising the lower end while reducing the upper end.

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Ford, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Ford's Analyst Ratings.
Ford traded at 6.8x forward earnings on October 22, below its five-year average of 7.8x and its early-2022 peak of nearly 13x.
At its October 30 closing price of $12.25, Ford traded at approximately 7x forward earnings and offered a regular dividend yield of 4.9%. Its valuation already reflects expectations for limited earnings growth in 2027, while improved cash generation supports the investment case. Risks remain, particularly weaker Ford Pro profitability and delays in initiatives expected to improve earnings in 2028. The dividend provides income while shareholders wait, although sustaining those payments depends on continued cash generation. Overall, Ford looks undervalued, making the recent gain a potential buying opportunity rather than a reason to sell.

Title: Jim Cramer Calls Ralph Lauren Stock Top Apparel Pick Before Thursday Earnings
Author: Darryn Pollock   Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:12 AM GMT+1 2 min read
Published: 2026-11-03T04:12:00+00:00
=== BODY ===
Jim Cramer named Ralph Lauren (RL) stock his favorite apparel pick ahead of its earnings report on Thursday, citing a 380% rally since late 2022 that has outpaced the S&P 500's roughly 110% gain.
Ralph Lauren holders face the print with that gain intact, while Tapestry (TPR), parent of Coach, fell more than 20% after its August report on guidance Cramer called merely in line. It reports the same morning.
Cramer said Ralph Lauren's sales compounded at 13% a year over the past five fiscal years, while adjusted earnings per share (EPS) compounded at 57%.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c0VXcG8TAIw
He credits a pivot to direct-to-consumer (DTC) sales and fewer wholesale outlets that he says watered down the brand, a shift he links to wider gross margins.
The company reported adjusted EPS of $4.59 and revenue of $1.96 billion for its fiscal first quarter on Aug. 6, beating Wall Street estimates on both, and raised its full-year outlook.
Management guided second-quarter revenue growth of 5% to 6%, excluding currency swings.
Analysts forecast adjusted EPS of about $4.22 for the quarter, up from $3.79 a year earlier.
Cramer said the shares slid in late August and September, when rising oil prices hit consumer names broadly. A Walmart sales miss in August had already raised questions about US consumer health.
BofA Securities analyst Kendall Toscano expects a beat-and-raise quarter, meaning earnings above forecasts and a higher outlook. He keeps a $450 price target, arguing higher-income shoppers remain resilient.
Analysts expect Tapestry to report adjusted EPS near $1.55. Cramer likes the Coach story, citing its accessible luxury niche and appeal to younger women.
Coach revenue rose 15% in the fiscal fourth quarter, while Kate Spade fell 7%, with management acknowledging that the Kate Spade turnaround is running slower than planned.
Thursday's reports will test whether premium accessories and apparel brands that raised prices, as Coach did on handbags, can keep demand if shoppers tighten. Cramer listed consumer spending among five themes in his 2026 stock picks.

Futures turned lower during the Asian session as Apple's losses spilled over into regional tech shares, adding to pressure on chipmakers and electronics firms.
Artificial intelligence startup Anthropic also weakened sentiment towards tech after it disclosed a sharp deterioration in revenue growth in the third quarter, raising more questions over the profitability of AI.
Wall Street fell on Monday, with the S&P 500 losing 0.5% in the first trading day of November as a rout in tech showed few signs of easing.
Caution before the midterm elections kept Wall Street on edge, especially as President Donald Trump and the Republican party face an uphill battle.
In-person voting is set to begin on Tuesday.
Recent opinion polls showed the Republicans risk losing their majority in both chambers of Congress, amid growing voter discontent over high fuel prices, corruption, and a protracted war with Iran. A Reuters/IPSOS poll showed Trump's approval rating at a record low going into the midterms.
Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »
A Republican loss in Congress presents more headwinds for Trump in enacting his agenda. The president is expected to resort to more executive measures in such a scenario, heralding much more regulatory uncertainty for markets.
Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL) fell as much as 3% in aftermarket trade after the iPhone maker forecast slightly below-consensus gross margin for the current quarter, citing mounting headwinds from soaring global memory prices.
Apple guided gross margin of 45% to 46%, below Street expectations of 46.9%.
CEO John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook in September, said rising memory costs were "unprecedented," and that prices were likely to increase in this quarter and beyond.
The tech giant guided a slowdown in revenue from its Services segment, which is its second-biggest breadwinner behind the iPhone. Apple flagged headwinds from unfavorable currency markets, regulations, and a sustained slowdown in mobile gaming.
Still, Apple beat top and bottom-line estimates for the September quarter, aided chiefly by strong sales of its new iPhone 18 line. The company's first foldable– Duo– was also launched to outsized demand in October, although Apple warned that supplies of the foldable were likely to be constrained in the near-term.
Apple announced a new version of its Siri voice assistance, but offered few cues on its plans to integrate more artificial intelligence in its services.
The iPhone maker is widely regarded as a large-cap hedge against artificial intelligence, given its relatively low exposure to the technology. This benefited the company's shares in recent weeks, amid a broader AI-driven wipeout in tech.
Apple recently overtook Nvidia to reclaim its spot as the most valuable publicly listed company in the world.
Among other aftermarket movers, Palantir Technologies Inc (NASDAQ:PLTR) fell 3.1% in aftermarket trade after its blowout third-quarter earnings still failed to meet some lofty expectations. The AI and data firm also faced profit-taking after a strong run-up this year.

Title: US Stock Market Fails To Recover as $700 Billion Comeback Collapses
Author: Lockridge Okoth   Mon, November 2, 2026 at 11:56 PM GMT+1 2 min read
Published: 2026-11-02T22:56:17+00:00
=== BODY ===
Wall Street appeared ready to recover from October's $2 trillion technology stock wipeout on Monday. Within hours, roughly $700 billion in fresh market gains had evaporated.
The S&P 500 surged as much as 1.1% in morning trading before closing down 0.5%. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.1%, extending last week's brutal AI stock selloff.
The reversal came shortly after CNBC host Jim Cramer posted on X:
He was referring to Marvell's $115 billion acquisition of Lumentum. But the timing quickly revived jokes about Cramer's famously mixed market predictions.
The morning optimism came from the Middle East.
Oil prices dropped to $104 as possible US-Iran peace talks raised hopes of cheaper energy and easing inflation.
Stocks initially jumped. The Nasdaq 100 gained around 1.3%, while the Dow climbed more than 1%.
But investors soon returned to the same concern that erased more than $2 trillion from the Nasdaq 100 during October: How much longer can Big Tech keep spending billions on AI without delivering sufficient returns?
Oracle plunged nearly 9% after announcing plans to raise $20 billion through stock and bond sales to fund its AI expansion. Marvell lost almost 13%.
Meanwhile, White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett dismissed fears of an AI financing crisis.
"There's so much cash in the ecosystem that I think that people should be reassured," Hassett said.
Interestingly, nearly 70% of S&P 500 companies finished higher. The weakness remained concentrated in major technology stocks.
As for Cramer's supposed curse, the Inverse Cramer ETF, designed to bet against his recommendations, lost 15% before closing in 2024.
Investors now face Tuesday's US midterm elections and Friday's jobs report, with confidence in the AI trade already shaken.

Sigma Lithium prices US$125 million, 5-year convertible bond offering due 2031, upsized by 25%.
Primary use of net proceeds: repay Senior Secured Debt with Synergy Capital.
Lowers cash interest costs enabling the Company to build operating cash flow: a fixed coupon of 7.00% p.a. replaces a floating coupon of 11.45% p.a. (SOFR, 4.5% + 6.95% p.a.)
Sets a healthy conversion premium of 25% over US$5.21, the Nasdaq closing price on November 2, 2026, resulting in a conversion price of US$6.51, without conversion during the first 12 months.
The convertible bond significantly extends repayment duration to 2031.
Greater financial flexibility for future growth plans by replacing secured borrowing with unsecured financing, with Synergy Capital's security to be released upon repayment.
Significantly reduces short-term debt by approximately 80%, from US$125 million
The successful transaction is a result of the Company's consistent track record of strengthening its balance sheet, demonstrating financial discipline over the last two years:
More than US$90 million in debt repaid since 2Q 24 through cash generation.
Total debt reduced by approximately 40% over two years, to US$125 million on October 21, 2026.
Sigma Lithium has been self-funded since July 2023, without any equity issuance since 2021.
The transaction demonstrates strong investor support for continued execution of Sigma's management strategy and growth plans.
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 2, 2026) - Sigma Lithium Corporation (NASDAQ: SGML) (ASX: SAU) (TSXV: SGML) (BVMF: S2GM34) ("Sigma Lithium" or the "Company"), the largest producer of industrial-mineral lithium oxide concentrate in the Americas¹, is pleased to announce that the upsized US$125 million offering (the "Offering") of senior unsecured convertible bonds due 2031 (the "Bonds"), convertible into CHESS Depositary Interests (the "CDIs"), listed on ASX Limited, over common shares in the Company, which launched on November 2, 2026, has priced. The Offering was upsized by 25% from the initially launched US$100 million. The Bonds will bear a fixed coupon of 7.00% p.a. The conversion premium is confirmed at 25% over US$5.21, being the closing price of the common shares on the Nasdaq on November 2, 2026 (the "Reference Price"), resulting in a conversion price of US$6.51.
Each CDI represents one common share of Sigma Lithium. The Bonds were offered solely outside Canada and the United States to non-U.S. persons, in accordance with OSC Rule 72-503 and in reliance on Regulation S under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended. The net proceeds will refinance in full the Company's Senior Secured Debt with Synergy Capital and extend its debt maturity profile to 2031.
The Offering, the Company's first convertible bond issuance, refinances Sigma Lithium's largest near-term debt obligation and aligns its debt profile with the planned production expansion. The Senior Secured Debt with Synergy Capital matures in June 2027, following the maturity extension announced on October 23, 2026. The repayment of this debt:
Significantly lengthens the recently extended maturity from June 2027 to 2031, reducing short-term debt by approximately 80%, from US$125 million on a pro forma basis.
Replaces a floating rate of SOFR + 6.95% p.a. of the Senior Secured Debt with a fixed 7.00% p.a. coupon, lowering and fixing cash interest costs.
Replaces secured debt with unsecured debt, releasing Corporate Security tied up in connection with the previous Senior Secured Debt.
Moves the earliest repayment date to 2029 (investor put) and final maturity to 2031.
The conversion is set at a 25% premium to the Reference Price and is not available for the first 12 months after closing, other than in limited circumstances.
The Company intends to use the net proceeds to repay in full the outstanding amounts under the Senior Secured Debt agreement with Synergy Capital. The balance of proceeds will be applied to growth capital expenditure and general corporate purposes.
Size: US$125 million (upsized by 25% from US$100 million);
Coupon: 7.00% p.a. fixed, payable quarterly in arrears;
Maturity: approximately November 2031, 5 years from the closing date of the Bonds (the "Closing Date"). Unless previously redeemed, repurchased or converted in accordance with their terms, the Bonds will be redeemed at 100% of principal plus accrued but unpaid interest;
Investor put: holders may require redemption of 100% of principal at the end of year 3 (approximately November 2029);
Conversion: into CDIs (one CDI per common share) at a conversion price of US$6.51 (the "Conversion Price"), being a 25% premium to the Reference Price. Conversion is available from 12 months after the Closing Date to 5 business days before maturity, subject to certain customary exceptions;
Dividend protection: full adjustment of the Conversion Price for dividends paid by the Company; and
Ranking: unsubordinated and unsecured obligations of Sigma Lithium.
Following pricing on November 2, 2026, the Offering is expected to close on or about November 16, 2026, subject to all necessary regulatory and stock exchange approvals, including TSX Venture Exchange approval.
The Company has applied for the Bonds to be listed on the Vienna MTF operated by the Vienna Stock Exchange (or an appropriate alternative exchange), with the listing of the Bonds expected to become effective as soon as reasonably practicable after the Closing Date.
The Bonds are solely being offered for sale in jurisdictions outside Canada pursuant to applicable regulatory requirements and in accordance with OSC Rule 72-503 – Distributions Outside Canada ("OSC Rule 72-503"), provided it is understood that no prospectus filing or comparable obligation, ongoing reporting requirement or requisite regulatory or governmental approval arises in such jurisdictions. The Bonds and any underlying securities thereunder, issued to investors outside of Canada pursuant to OSC Rule 72-503 will not be subject to a hold period under Canadian securities laws.
Sigma Lithium Corporation (NASDAQ: SGML) (ASX: SAU) (TSXV: SGML) (BVMF: S2GM34) ("Sigma Lithium" or "the Company") is the largest industrial-mineral producer of lithium oxide concentrate in the Americas¹ and is dedicated to industrializing socially and environmentally sustainable lithium materials to supply global producers of batteries for energy security. The Company runs one of the world's largest lithium production sites—the fifth largest industrial-mineral complex for lithium oxide concentrate—at its Grota do Cirilo operation in Brazil. Sigma Lithium currently has a nameplate capacity to industrialize 330,000 tonnes of lithium oxide concentrate on an annualized basis at its mine and state-of-the-art Cleantech Industrial Plant.
Sigma Lithium is at the forefront of environmental and social sustainability in the battery materials supply chain. Its Cleantech Industrial Plant combines nearly 100% water reuse, zero use of toxic chemicals, no tailings mud dams, and 100% renewable electricity. For more than three years, Sigma Lithium has recorded no lost-time accidents.
The Company plans to resume its Phase 2 expansion in 2027, which is designed to nearly double annual production capacity to 580,000 tonnes. It also plans a Phase 3 expansion to increase capacity further to 830,000 tonnes. For more information about Sigma Lithium, visit our website.

CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV), a specialized cloud computing provider for generative AI workloads, closed at $50.15, down 8.60%. Premarket partnership news with CrowdStrike faded as leverage concerns weighed on the market, and investors are watching Nov. 10 earnings.
Trading volume reached 47.1M shares, coming in nearly 21% above its three-month average of 38.9M shares. CoreWeave IPO'd in 2025 and has grown 25% since going public.
The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) dropped 0.50% to 7,542, and the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX: ^IXIC) fell 1.07% to 25,164. Among peers in AI cloud infrastructure and specialized data center services, Oracle closed at $119.10, down 8.85%, and Nebius Group closed at $141.39, down 8.27%, underscoring weakness across chip-adjacent infrastructure names.
The latest price action in CoreWeave shows continued shareholder discomfort with the cloud stock's reliance on debt.
Although the expanded partnership with CrowdStrike is objectively good news for the company, the excitement over that deal was short-lived as the stock's downtrend continued.
Customer interest is not the issue. Demand for neocloud infrastructure is insatiable, as CoreWeave's backlog totaled $104 billion, not including Q3 customer commitments.
Still, that demand does the company little good if its ability to finance infrastructure builds remains in question. Considering that industry insiders like Elon Musk think many neoclouds will fail, CoreWeave is likely to remain under the gun for the foreseeable future.
In fairness, CoreWeave is not the only neocloud stock struggling, as both Nebius and Oracle also plunged. However, Oracle still has other legacy businesses, and Nebius is a profitable company with a debt level that's a fraction of CoreWeave's approximate $35 billion in obligations.
The real test for CoreWeave stock may come when it announces its earnings for the third quarter of 2026 on Nov. 10. Factors such as growth, capital expenditures, and debt levels will be where investors will probably focus.
If CoreWeave can continue building infrastructure, address its backlog, and service its debt, it may eventually win back investors' confidence. Nonetheless, any interruptions to this growth could be costly for CoreWeave, making investing in the stock a risky proposition at this time.

markets.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the lowest temperature reported at Paris-Le Bourget Airport (LFPB) on 3 Nov '26.

The qualifying value is the lowest temperature reported in the hourly temperature remark of any routine (METAR) observation for Paris-Le Bourget Airport (LFPB) on that date, in tenths of a degree Celsius as reported. A report whose line begins with SPECI is a special observation and does not count. Every other report is routine, including one issued off the nominal hour and one that carries no METAR or SPECI label.

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Celsius. The qualifying value is rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Celsius value determines which range contains it. For example, 13.9°C counts as 14°C; 17.4°C counts as 17°C; 16.5°C counts as 17°C; −1.7°C counts as −2°C; −8.5°C counts as −8°C.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be the routine observations for Paris-Le Bourget Airport (LFPB) published here:
https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=LFPB&format=raw&date=2026-11-04T02:00:00Z&hours=30

markets.description:
The 2026 WI-07 House election is currently expected to be held on November 3, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the specified election.

The "margin of victory" is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first-place and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

For purposes of this market, candidates nominated by the Democratic & Republican Parties will represent the options for "Democrat" and "Republican," respectively. Independent candidates will not represent options for either party. The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher margin bracket.

If two or more candidates tie for the most valid votes in this election, and the tie is between two candidates listed, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the candidate whose ballot-listed last name comes first in alphabetical order. If the tie is between a listed candidate and an unlisted candidate, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the listed candidate. If the tie is between two or more unlisted candidates, this market will resolve to "Other." If the listed candidate is represented in this market group as "Republican" or "Democrat" their ballot-listed last name will still be used for tiebreaking.

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the count has been made official.

If the election results are not known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official results of the 2026 WI-07 House election as published by the state electoral authority responsible for certifying the results of the election; however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

markets.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature reported at Beijing Capital International Airport (ZBAA) on 5 Nov '26.

The qualifying value is the highest temperature reported in the hourly temperature remark of any routine (METAR) observation for Beijing Capital International Airport (ZBAA) on that date, in tenths of a degree Celsius as reported. A report whose line begins with SPECI is a special observation and does not count. Every other report is routine, including one issued off the nominal hour and one that carries no METAR or SPECI label.

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Celsius. The qualifying value is rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Celsius value determines which range contains it. For example, 13.9°C counts as 14°C; 17.4°C counts as 17°C; 16.5°C counts as 17°C; −1.7°C counts as −2°C; −8.5°C counts as −8°C.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be the routine observations for Beijing Capital International Airport (ZBAA) published here:
https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=ZBAA&format=raw&date=2026-11-05T19:00:00Z&hours=30

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Celsius. The qualifying value is rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Celsius value determines which range contains it. For example, 13.9°C counts as 14°C; 17.4°C counts as 17°C; 16.5°C counts as 17°C; −1.7°C counts as −2°C; −8.5°C counts as −8°C.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be the routine observations for Malpensa Intl Airport (LIMC) published here:
https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=LIMC&format=raw&date=2026-11-04T02:00:00Z&hours=30

markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a kinetic strike is conducted on, or forceful seizure of control is taken of, a commercial ship within the defined area on the specified date, between 12:00 AM and 11:59 PM UTC. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The defined area consists of the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, and the Gulf of Oman. An incident occurring outside these three bodies of water will not qualify, including in the Arabian Sea, the Gulf of Aden, or the Red Sea.

No attribution is required. A qualifying incident will count regardless of the identity of the party responsible, regardless of whether any state or group claims responsibility, and regardless of whether responsibility is denied, disputed, or never established.

Attacks on military vessels will not be considered.

Missile/drone strikes targeting a ship that are intercepted or otherwise do not directly impact the vessel will not be considered, regardless of damage through debris.

Seize control refers to forcefully boarding and taking control of a commercial ship.

Qualifying incidents include, but are not limited to, drone and missile strikes, aerial bombings, and kinetic actions carried out by operatives in person. Damaged caused by mines will not qualify. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

The occurrence, location, and timing of a qualifying incident will be primarily determined based on a consensus of information available from the resolution sources. Where multiple sources conflict regarding the occurrence, location, or timing of a relevant incident, this market will remain open until the earlier of: i) the confirmation of the occurrence, location, and timing of the incident based on a consensus of information available from the resolution sources or ii) 3 full calendar days (UTC) from the date of the first credibly reported evidence of the incident. If this period would extend past the end date, this market will remain open to allow for 3 full calendar days to pass. If, at the end of the third calendar day, conflicting reports remain as to the occurrence, location, or timing of the incident, the incident will be judged on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the lowest temperature reported at Warsaw Chopin Airport (EPWA) on 3 Nov '26.

The qualifying value is the lowest temperature reported in the hourly temperature remark of any routine (METAR) observation for Warsaw Chopin Airport (EPWA) on that date, in tenths of a degree Celsius as reported. A report whose line begins with SPECI is a special observation and does not count. Every other report is routine, including one issued off the nominal hour and one that carries no METAR or SPECI label.

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Celsius. The qualifying value is rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Celsius value determines which range contains it. For example, 13.9°C counts as 14°C; 17.4°C counts as 17°C; 16.5°C counts as 17°C; −1.7°C counts as −2°C; −8.5°C counts as −8°C.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be the routine observations for Warsaw Chopin Airport (EPWA) published here:
https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=EPWA&format=raw&date=2026-11-04T02:00:00Z&hours=30

markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the State of Missouri enacts a law or constitutional provision that establishes a statewide moratorium on new data centers between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A statewide moratorium on new data centers refers to a binding policy with legal force that generally prohibits or suspends the approval, permitting, construction, grid interconnection, or operation of all new data centers, or a subset of data centers that includes all new data centers with an interconnection capacity above 100 MW per facility (requested or nameplate), throughout the state. Suspensions of tax incentives, exemption certifications, or economic development awards alone will not qualify, nor will a moratorium adopted by a local government or limited to part of the state. Specific exemptions (e.g., for specified applications, executed agreements, or interconnection requests) do not prevent a measure from generally applying to all new data centers, or a qualifying subset of new data centers, provided that data center approval, permitting, construction, grid interconnection, or operation is prohibited by default, rather than permitted subject to conditions or restrictions. Conditions on the resumption or termination of a suspension do not make a measure one that permits subject to conditions; a measure that suspends approvals, permitting, construction, or interconnection until a specified condition is satisfied qualifies.

Enactment occurs when a bill becomes law under the state's constitution and laws, whether by gubernatorial signature, veto override, becoming law without signature, approval at a statewide referendum election, or any other legal mechanism by which statutes can be enacted. For an initiated or referred statute or constitutional amendment, or other voter referendum, the relevant law is considered to have been enacted on the election day on which it was approved, as reflected in the certified results, regardless of when the measure is certified or takes effect. Passage by one or both chambers, or a Governor's announced intent to sign, is not enactment.

Executive orders, agency orders, and other measures which are not statutory or constitutional do not qualify as enactment regardless of legal force. A provision removed by line-item veto is not enacted unless the veto is overridden as to that item. The operative text of the measure at enactment controls; provisions amended out before enactment do not qualify.

The moratorium provision must be mandatory on its face. A statute that merely authorizes a state agency or the Governor to impose a moratorium at their discretion does not qualify. A statute that directs suspension of approvals or interconnection upon a specified condition qualifies only if the condition is objectively determinable and is not deferred to be determined by the implementing agency's findings, certifications, or completion of its own proceedings.

This market resolves based on the date of enactment, not the effective date. Resolution will not be affected by failure to implement a law, judicial invalidation, repeal, or expiry that follows a relevant enactment, or an effective date that comes after the date of enactment.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the state government of Missouri; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

If two or more candidates tie for the most valid votes in this election, and the tie is between two candidates listed, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the candidate whose ballot-listed last name comes first in alphabetical order. If the tie is between a listed candidate and an unlisted candidate, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the listed candidate. If the tie is between two or more unlisted candidates, this market will resolve to "Other." If the listed candidate is represented in this market group as "Republican" or "Democrat" their ballot-listed last name will still be used for tiebreaking.

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the count has been made official.

markets.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature reported at Malpensa Intl Airport (LIMC) on 3 Nov '26.

The qualifying value is the highest temperature reported in the hourly temperature remark of any routine (METAR) observation for Malpensa Intl Airport (LIMC) on that date, in tenths of a degree Celsius as reported. A report whose line begins with SPECI is a special observation and does not count. Every other report is routine, including one issued off the nominal hour and one that carries no METAR or SPECI label.

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Celsius. The qualifying value is rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Celsius value determines which range contains it. For example, 13.9°C counts as 14°C; 17.4°C counts as 17°C; 16.5°C counts as 17°C; −1.7°C counts as −2°C; −8.5°C counts as −8°C.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be the routine observations for Malpensa Intl Airport (LIMC) published here:
https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=LIMC&format=raw&date=2026-11-04T02:00:00Z&hours=30

markets.description:
The 2026 Alabama gubernatorial election is currently expected to be held on November 3, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the specified election.

The "margin of victory" is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first-place and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

For purposes of this market, candidates nominated by the Democratic & Republican Parties will represent the options for "Democrat" and "Republican," respectively. Independent candidates will not represent options for either party. The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher margin bracket.

If two or more candidates tie for the most valid votes in this election, and the tie is between two candidates listed, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the candidate whose ballot-listed last name comes first in alphabetical order. If the tie is between a listed candidate and an unlisted candidate, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the listed candidate. If the tie is between two or more unlisted candidates, this market will resolve to "Other." If the listed candidate is represented in this market group as "Republican" or "Democrat" their ballot-listed last name will still be used for tiebreaking.

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the count has been made official.

If the election results are not known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official results of the 2026 Alabama gubernatorial election as published by the state electoral authority responsible for certifying the results of the election; however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

markets.description:
The 2026 AZ-01 House election is currently expected to be held on November 3, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the specified election.

The "margin of victory" is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first-place and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

For purposes of this market, candidates nominated by the Democratic & Republican Parties will represent the options for "Democrat" and "Republican," respectively. Independent candidates will not represent options for either party. The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher margin bracket.

If two or more candidates tie for the most valid votes in this election, and the tie is between two candidates listed, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the candidate whose ballot-listed last name comes first in alphabetical order. If the tie is between a listed candidate and an unlisted candidate, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the listed candidate. If the tie is between two or more unlisted candidates, this market will resolve to "Other." If the listed candidate is represented in this market group as "Republican" or "Democrat" their ballot-listed last name will still be used for tiebreaking.

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the count has been made official.

If the election results are not known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official results of the 2026 AZ-01 House election as published by the state electoral authority responsible for certifying the results of the election; however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may also be used.
markets.question: Will the Republican Party candidate win the 2026 AZ-01 House election by 0%-3%?

markets.description:
This market refers to the LoL Quarterfinal 2 match between Karmine Corp and T1 in the Worlds Playoffs, initially scheduled for November 4, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET.

This market will resolve to "Over" if Karmine Corp and T1 play 5 or more games in this series.

If fewer than 5 games are played, this market will resolve to "Under".

Games won by forfeit, disqualification, walkover, or default are counted towards the total, provided that the match is completed.

If the match is canceled (not played at all for any reason) or ends in a tie, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If the match is postponed, it must be rescheduled to a start time on or before November 18, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET (14 calendar days after the originally scheduled start of November 4, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET). If, by that deadline, the most recently announced rescheduled start time is on or before the deadline, this market resolves based on the result of the match as played. Otherwise, this market resolves 50-50, regardless of whether the match is subsequently played.

The match is considered to have begun once live play begins in its first map or game. Warmup rounds and knife rounds do not count as the start of the match. A round forced live because a team did not ready up or resume play within the allotted time does not count as the start of the match if that team forfeits before the next round begins.

If the match begins and one team wins due to the opponent's match forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, the match will count as completed.

In that case, any remaining games required to decide the match, including a game in progress or not yet started, will be counted as won by the winning team.

If the match ends due to the clinching game being forfeited this will count as a completed match.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

markets.description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the listed bank fails between market creation and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

For the purposes of this market, the listed bank will be considered to have “failed” if any of the following occurs under the bank’s applicable legal or regulatory framework, within the listed date range:

- The listed bank’s primary banking regulator formally declares the institution insolvent or non-viable, or withdraws or revokes the bank’s license or authorization, and such determination initiates or directly results in resolution, liquidation, wind-down, or transfer actions.
- The listed bank enters a court-ordered liquidation, statutory resolution regime, or regulator-mandated wind-down, including the use of resolution tools such as bail-ins, forced asset transfers, or the establishment of a bridge bank.
- A government or resolution authority intervenes in a manner that wipes out or subordinates existing equity of the listed bank and transfers effective control of the bank to the state or a designated resolution authority, with continued operations dependent on official intervention.
- The listed bank publicly defaults on a payment obligation, including derivatives margin, repo, or physical commodity delivery, and such default is formally acknowledged by the bank’s primary regulator or resolution authority and directly results in the initiation of resolution, liquidation, license withdrawal, or regulator-mandated transfer of the bank.
- The listed bank is subject to a compulsory merger, acquisition, or transfer of all or substantially all of its assets and liabilities ordered or directed by its primary banking regulator or resolution authority due to the bank’s financial condition or to prevent failure, regardless of whether a formal insolvency declaration or immediate equity wipeout is publicly announced at the time of transfer.

If there is a potential failure of the listed bank within this market’s date range and a qualifying regulatory or court action has occurred but has not yet been fully published by the relevant authority, this market may remain open until April 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET to allow for confirmation. If no qualifying failure is confirmed by that date, this market will resolve to “No.”

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements, filings, or actions by the listed bank’s primary banking regulator or resolution authority; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.
markets.question: Will US Bank fail by end of 2026?

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Futuro Nazionale receives at least the listed percentage of total valid votes in the next Italian general elections. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Only the vote totals from the Italy (excluding Valle d’Aosta) will be considered in this market. Votes from outside Italy or from the Valle d’Aosta constituency will not count.

If the specified party runs as a joint list (lista congiunta / simbolo congiunto) with any other parties in the next Italian general elections, the total votes received by the joint list will be considered the votes received by the specified party for the purposes of this market.

Percentage of total valid votes will be calculated by dividing the total number of valid votes received by the specified party or its joint list by the total number of valid votes in the specified election.

This market will not consider the valid vote totals of any coalition (coalizione) that the specified party joins. Only votes received by the specified party, or any applicable joint list, will count for resolution of this market.

If the specified party changes its name or otherwise reconstitutes in a way which functionally represents the same entity in the next Italian general elections, this market will consider the new name or reconstitution as an extension of the original specified party.

If Italy does not hold general elections, or the results of the next Italian general elections are not known definitively, by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “No”. If the specified party disbands by, or otherwise does not contest the next Italian general elections, this market will resolve to “No”.

The 2026 New Mexico gubernatorial election is currently expected to be held on November 3, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the specified election.

The "margin of victory" is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first-place and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

For purposes of this market, candidates nominated by the Democratic & Republican Parties will represent the options for "Democrat" and "Republican," respectively. Independent candidates will not represent options for either party. The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher margin bracket.

If two or more candidates tie for the most valid votes in this election, and the tie is between two candidates listed, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the candidate whose ballot-listed last name comes first in alphabetical order. If the tie is between a listed candidate and an unlisted candidate, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the listed candidate. If the tie is between two or more unlisted candidates, this market will resolve to "Other." If the listed candidate is represented in this market group as "Republican" or "Democrat" their ballot-listed last name will still be used for tiebreaking.

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the count has been made official.

If the election results are not known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official results of the 2026 New Mexico gubernatorial election as published by the state electoral authority responsible for certifying the results of the election; however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Anduril's private market valuation, as measured by the NPM Price reported by Nasdaq Private Market, LLC (NPM) for any date between market creation and December 31, 2026, reaches or exceeds the listed amount. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

NPM Prices are published for trading days only and are updated once daily at 1:00 PM ET on the following calendar day.

If NPM has not published relevant data for all business dates in the specified period by 1:00 PM ET on January 1, 2027, this market may remain open until 11:59 PM ET on January 4, 2027. If no further data is released by that time, the market will resolve according to the data available.

If NPM ceases publishing relevant data prior to the end of the specified period, this market will resolve based on the NPM data published for the period prior to the cessation of coverage, as well as any applicable public market capitalization data following an IPO or direct listing.

If the company completes an IPO or direct listing before the end of the specified period, this market will consider, in addition to the relevant NPM valuations published between market creation and the IPO or direct listing date, the valuation implied by the official IPO or direct listing price, and the company's public market capitalization between the IPO or direct listing date and the end of the specified period.

Public market capitalization will be determined using the highest/lowest official regular-hours trading price published for the company's primary listed common equity on its primary exchange for any trading day during the specified period, multiplied by the company's total outstanding common shares at the relevant time.

If the listed company merges with or acquires another entity and remains the parent company, no change to resolution methodology applies.

If the listed company is acquired, merges into another entity and is no longer the surviving parent company, or otherwise ceases to exist as an independent entity prior to the end of the period, only NPM valuations and applicable public market capitalizations achieved prior to completion of the transaction will be considered for resolution. No transaction, acquisition, or merger consideration will be considered for resolution.

The resolution source for this market is NPM data published here (https://fe.secondmarket.com/companies/company-c62b8140-fdeb-428d-a9a6-d04eb3b24b49/data). The resolution source for any period following an IPO, direct listing, or relevant corporate action, will be official exchange trading data and publicly reported share counts.

Revisions to previously published NPM data made after their initial release will not be considered, unless made to correct clearly erroneous data.
